PB[An Immortal]

DT[ca. 800]
GC["In a Tang poem by Meng Qiao (751-814) which was modeled after
a Daoist folktale, a woodcutter comes across two boys playing a game.
He becomes so absorbed in the game that by the time it is over his
axe handle has rotted away. As he crosses a bridge on his return home,
he sees a rainbow and realizes he is returning from the Other Side,
and had been watching two immortals." (Peter Shotwell, Go! More than a game)

The story is much older, perhaps from the 4th century, and then refers
to an unspecified game.

"The text says: Long ago Wang Shi went into Rotten Axe-handle mountain
in Qu province to gather firewood. There he met immortals playing go.
He recorded the game and passed it down to posterity. W plays first.
145 moves each. B captures 22 white stones. W captures 9 black stones.
B has 5 groups, W has 3 groups.
Territory - captured - group tax: B: 37-9-10=18, W: 45-22-6=17." (GoGoD)

See also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranka_(legend)
and http://senseis.xmp.net/?Ranka]
